source_text:
12.1 Εἰς τὸ τέλος,
ψαλμὸς τῷ ∆αυίδ. ̔Υπόθεσις Εὐσεβίου. ∆ιὰ τὸ τέλος, τὸ παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ, πάντα τὰ πρὸ
τοῦ τέλους ἀνδρικῶς ἠγωνίζετο· τὸ δὲ τέλος καρπὸς ὁ τῶν πό νων, ζωὴν αἰώνιον
καὶ βασιλείαν οὐρανῶν τοῖς γνησίως ἀγωνιζομένοις προξενῶν. ̓Επεὶ τοίνυν καὶ ὁ
∆αυὶδ τούτων ει ς η ν, εἰς μὲν τὸ τέλος τῷ Θεῷ τὸν ψαλμὸν καὶ τὴν ᾠδὴν ἀνέπεμπε.
Κατὰ δὲ τὴν ἀρχὴν, ὡσανεὶ ε τι ἀγωνιζόμενος, τὰς πρώτας προέφερε φωνάς·
pass_a_gloss: Unto the end, a-psalm to-David. Hypothesis of-Eusebius. Because-of the end, the [end] beside God, all-the-things before the end manfully he-was-contending; and the end [is] the fruit of-the labors, eternal life and kingdom of-heavens to-the genuinely contending procuring. Since then also the David of-these one was, unto on-the-one-hand the end to-God the psalm and the ode he-was-sending-up. But according-to the beginning, as-if still contending, the first he-was-putting-forth utterances.
pass_b_english: “Unto the end, a psalm to David.” Hypothesis of Eusebius.

Because of the end, the one with God, he contended manfully in all the things before the end; and the end is the fruit of the labors, procuring eternal life and the kingdom of the heavens for those who genuinely contend.
Since then David also was one of these, he sent up the psalm and the ode to God unto the end. But at the beginning, as if still contending, he put forth the first utterances.

choices.why: LXX inscription. τέλος here is the end with God, the fruit of the labors, not a mere close of the psalm.
rejected: At the end of the psalm

choices.term: πάντα τὰ πρὸ τοῦ τέλους ἀνδρικῶς ἠγωνίζετο
choices.english: he contended manfully in all the things before the end
choices.why: ἠγωνίζετο is 3sg; πάντα τὰ πρὸ τοῦ τέλους is the field of the contest, not the subject.
rejected: all things before the end manfully struggled

choices.english: David also was one of these
choices.why: One of those who genuinely contend. OCR ει ς η ν. Not ‘David wrote these’.
rejected: David was the first of them

choices.term: ὡσανεὶ ἔτι ἀγωνιζόμενος, τὰς πρώτας προέφερε φωνάς
choices.english: as if still contending, he put forth the first utterances
choices.why: ἔτι is still. The first utterances are the opening of the psalm, which 12.2 continues. Not ‘he first offered voices’.
rejected: as if struggling, he first offered voices

anf_compare.notes: ANF lacks this Greek catena as reading English.
